survey: A sci-fi astronaut helmet on a display stand, sitting on a light grey shelf or table, seen at three-quarter view. Main parts: (1) a white spherical helmet shell that turns slightly to the left of the camera; (2) a large oval amber visor set into the front-left of the shell; (3) a chrome tube rim framing the visor; (4) a chrome neck ring at the bottom of the sphere, where the helmet seats into (5) a round white base with a red band. The base sits flat on the shelf top, well inside its edge, and has a contact shadow, so it is properly supported. The sphere seats evenly into the neck ring. The shell reads as round and the base as a true cylinder. There are no cables, hoses or loose parts, and no invented glows or gadgets. The visor follows the curve of the shell, and as a helmet on a display stand the object makes sense.

errors.where: Chrome visor rim, right side (about the 3 o'clock position)
errors.what: The rim tube does not close into a continuous ring. A visible cut or step breaks it, so the two ends of the tube meet offset instead of forming one smooth loop. The visor glass edge also has a small notch at the same spot. A real visor frame would be one unbroken seal around the glass.

fix: Make the chrome visor rim one continuous, seamless tube ring around the whole oval visor, with no break, step or notch on the right side. The amber glass should meet the rim evenly all the way around.
